summary: This attempt closes the three findings that landed after build 1 passed, and changes no src. O-025: the twinned path-open rule now matches the ANSI forms ([AW]?) and NtQuery(Full)?AttributesFile. A second pattern catches the entry-point name as a string, so an import renamed through `EntryPoint = "CreateFileW"` or a `NativeLibrary.GetExport` lookup now fires. Plant F26 was added, rules-parity reads 29 patterns and AGREE, and the harness shows 56 of 56 AS-RECORDED. O-024: the rule's `because` and the Fact's doc no longer claim the compiler holds Kernel32.cs. A new Fact counts Kernel32.cs's path calls; a planted extra import fails it. O-023: eng/read-window.ps1 gained a `-DefaultErrorMode` launch (CREATE_DEFAULT_ERROR_MODE, created suspended so the child's error mode can be read). With it the published exe ran against the empty removable drives E:\ and F:\ with child error mode 0x0. Both ended RootUnreadable with error 21 in about 9 ms and exited 0 within 2 s, with no hang, so no box appeared. Full suite: 414 of 414 passed, and the repro command exits 0.

files.why: PathOpensGoOnlyThroughTheGuardedOpen: the call pattern is widened to [AW]? plus (Nt|Zw)Query(Full)?AttributesFile, and a second must_not_match matches the same names as a string literal (R2-m2). The `because` now says the compiler holds SynchronousIoCancel.cs but not Kernel32.cs, which review and a counting Fact hold (m1).
The twin Fact carries the same two patterns (the string pattern as a verbatim literal with doubled quotes, which rules-parity reads), and its doc comment is reworded to match the yaml.

New Fact Kernel32MakesOnlyThePathCallsThatRunInsideTheScope. It runs the rule's two patterns over Kernel32.cs's code lines, comments aside, and requires exactly CreateFile, CreateFileW x2, GetDiskFreeSpaceEx x2 and GetDiskFreeSpaceExW. It sits outside ArchitectureRulesTests, so the parity counts do not move. Adds a FindRepo helper in the house idiom and a using for System.Text.RegularExpressions.
Row F26 plants a new Native/Win32Paths.cs that imports CreateFileW through EntryPoint on a method named OpenPath; it must fire in both engines. The _note is updated to 43 rows, 26 of which must fire.

New -DefaultErrorMode switch. It starts the app suspended with CREATE_DEFAULT_ERROR_MODE, reads the child's error mode through NtQueryInformationProcess(ProcessDefaultHardErrorMode) with bit 0 flipped back, prints `ERRORMODE 0x..` before `EXIT`, then resumes the app. Without the switch the Start-Process path and the output are unchanged.

obligations.how: The launch this check needs could not be made before: this shell's own process error mode measures 0x8003, so a Start-Process child inherits SEM_FAILCRITICALERRORS and can never show a box. I added `-DefaultErrorMode` to eng/read-window.ps1. It uses CREATE_DEFAULT_ERROR_MODE and prints the child's error mode; I checked the bit inversion against GetErrorMode on this process (raw 0x8002, which reads back as 0x8003). A control run on a temp tree gave ERRORMODE 0x0 and Completed. I confirmed E:\ and F:\ are Removable with IsReady=False, then ran the freshly published exe on each: ERRORMODE 0x0, EXIT 0 after 2 s, core.status RootUnreadable, rootError 21, elapsedMs 9 and 8, and the window read 'Could not read E:\' / 'The device is not ready. (Windows error 21)'. There was no TIMEOUT, so no box held the open. As the disposition said, I did not add the opt-in Fact. Validate-slice can re-run the same command. Not shown: that this check fails on the pre-fix exe. See follow_ups.

I reworded the fitness.yaml `because` and the ArchitectureRulesTests doc. The compiler holds SynchronousIoCancel.cs, whose only path call is Kernel32.CreateFile and which takes the scope. It does not hold Kernel32.cs: review does, backed by a count. I also added the optional count Fact, Kernel32MakesOnlyThePathCallsThatRunInsideTheScope, in FailCriticalErrorsTests, outside the twinned Facts. It passes on the tree. Mutation check: I added `private const string PlantedPathCall = "GetFileAttributesExW";` to Kernel32.cs and the Fact failed, naming that line. The file was restored, with a matching hash.

In both the yaml and the xUnit Fact, `W?` became `[AW]?`, and a second pattern matches the path-taking names as a string literal. Checked with .NET Regex (Multiline): the renamed EntryPoint import, CreateFileA, FindFirstFileExA, GetFileAttributesExA, GetDiskFreeSpaceExA, NtQueryAttributesFile and NativeLibrary.GetExport(..., "CreateFileW") were all False under the old pattern and are all True now. The CreateFileW( and NtOpenFile( controls still fire. GetFileInformationByHandleEx, GetVolumeInformationByHandle, the GetVolumeInformationByHandleW entry point and cref="Kernel32.CreateFile" stay quiet. src/ has hits only in the two excepted files. Plant F26 was added. rules-parity: AGREE, 12 facts from 16 twinned entries and 29 patterns (derived, not literal), exit 0 under pwsh and powershell.exe. RuleCases C-001 to C-005 all held. Harness: 56 rows, 56 AS-RECORDED, F26 fires in both engines, 0 stray hits, exit 0.

I ran the exact repro command, `pwsh -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File eng/dotnet.ps1 test tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests.csproj --filter "FullyQualifiedName~FailCriticalErrorsTests.TheScannersRootOpenAndSizeProbeRunWithTheCriticalErrorBoxOff"`: 1 passed, exit 0. This obligation belongs to validate-slice, which runs it again.

NestedScopesUnwindInOrder and the restore Facts (the preset 0x0/0x2/0x1 Theory, failed opens, cancelled/refused/throwing opens, concurrent dedicated threads) pass in the full suite, 414 of 414. src did not change in this attempt. Validate-slice owns the final discharge.

cases.test_name: FsAnalyser.Core.Tests.LinkTests, HardlinkTests, OnDiskSizeTests, LongPathTests, UnreadableFolderTests (counting-rule suite, unchanged)

deviations: O-025: R2-m2's fix asked only for `[AW]?` in the call alternation, and put NtQuery(Full)?AttributesFile and the Zw forms in the new string pattern. I gave both patterns the same name list: (Nt|Zw)(Create|Open)File and (Nt|Zw)Query(Full)?AttributesFile appear in the call pattern too. The finding itself names NtQueryAttributesFile as a call that escapes, and with only `[AW]?` a direct `NtQueryAttributesFile(` call would still pass. ZwQueryAttributesFile is the one name added beyond the finding.

O-023: the disposition aimed the empty-drive run at validate-slice, and the design has no launcher change. I added `-DefaultErrorMode` to eng/read-window.ps1 because without it the check cannot be made. This shell's process error mode measures 0x8003, and the existing Start-Process launch passes that to the app, so a box could never appear and 'no box' would prove nothing. CREATE_DEFAULT_ERROR_MODE is the launch the disposition named. Without the switch the script's behaviour and output are unchanged; I checked by running it on a temp tree.
not_built: The optional opt-in Fact that scans an empty removable drive when one is present. The M1 disposition said not to add it, because it would skip on machines without such a drive and the design's tests are never skipped. The check is the read-window.ps1 -DefaultErrorMode run instead.

Handle-based calls after media is pulled mid-scan (listing, GetFileInformationByHandleEx, GetVolumeInformationByHandleW) are still outside the scope. This is design case C-014, non-material, and is still an open question for a person.

The regex ban on `new`/`default` CriticalErrorBoxOff, as in attempt 1: the disposition judged it unreliable. `new()` fails to compile through [Obsolete(error: true)], and Kernel32.CreateFile refuses a `default` scope at runtime.

tests.note: 26 passed, 0 failed: the new Kernel32 count Fact, the widened PathOpensGoOnlyThroughTheGuardedOpen, and RuleCopiesAgree (parity).

tests.note: All 8 escapes (renamed EntryPoint import, CreateFileA, FindFirstFileExA, GetFileAttributesExA, GetDiskFreeSpaceExA, NtQueryAttributesFile, NativeLibrary.GetExport by name) went from False to True. The controls CreateFileW( and NtOpenFile( fire under both. The 4 quiet inputs stay quiet. The renamed call site itself (Win.OpenPath(...)) matches nowhere; its import declaration is what fires.

tests.command: pwsh one-off: NtQueryInformationProcess(self, ProcessDefaultHardErrorMode) against GetErrorMode
tests.note: GetErrorMode=0x8003, raw=0x8002, raw^1=0x8003. This confirms the launcher's inversion. It also shows this shell passes SEM_FAILCRITICALERRORS on to any Start-Process child.
Control: ERRORMODE 0x0, EXIT 0, core Completed (1 file, 2 folders, 7 bytes).

Beforehand, E:\ was Removable with IsReady=False. ERRORMODE 0x0, EXIT 0 after 2 s (no TIMEOUT, so no box held the open). core {status RootUnreadable, rootError 21, files 0, elapsedMs 9}. Window: 'Could not read E:\' / 'The device is not ready. (Windows error 21)'.

Beforehand, F:\ was Removable with IsReady=False. ERRORMODE 0x0, EXIT 0 after 2 s. core {status RootUnreadable, rootError 21, elapsedMs 8}. Window: 'Could not read F:\' / 'The device is not ready. (Windows error 21)'.
The default launch without the switch is unchanged: the first line is EXIT 0, then the report JSON, core Completed.
Full default-filter suite: 414 passed (413 plus the new Fact), 0 failed, 0 skipped, 24 s.
The engine's repro command: 1 passed, exit 0.

follow_ups: Nobody has measured that the empty-drive check can fail. I did not run the pre-fix exe (uat 14acea3) with -DefaultErrorMode on E:\, because if the fix matters that run puts a modal 'insert a disk' box on the person's screen. So 'no box' today rests on the fix plus the assumption that this card reader raises one without it. A person can run it once, ready to dismiss the box, to settle that.

The design's open question is still undecided: should handle-based calls after media removal come into scope? The candidate answer is a process-wide SetErrorMode(SEM_FAILCRITICALERRORS) at App startup (review m1, deferred), or a one-line `using` per call.

The design record still has would_force_resynthesis: true on the per-open cost question (measured at about 37 ns per pair against 15.8 µs per open). Its key_decision rejecting a process-wide call should be restated on the grounds in m1's disposition.

At merge, check that the engine does not re-add a '# settled by SL-077' block under the design's prose rule name. It would duplicate the twinned entry (HF-008), and F24, F25 and F26 would then need also_settled.
